dossier.public_summary: The 0.89-day dip appears on the target star but has the same period as the star's strong 0.89-day spot rotation and shows a 9072 ppm phase-curve swing as large as the dip itself. Its long duration is inconsistent with a planet for this small M dwarf, and the dip depth is tiny compared with the 22729-29682 ppm spot signal. The periodic dimming is best explained as a rotational alias of the active M dwarf's own variability, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: A sinusoidal swing of the same size as the 7680 ppm dip (9072 ppm) at this period is much larger than a planetary phase curve and shows coherent modulation, indicating the 1.24-hour modulation is the star's own signal, not a transit.

Signal period is essentially 1x the measured spot rotation period (998.06% of it) on a very spotted M dwarf. Depth ~7680 ppm is only ~34% of the 22729-29682 ppm spot variability, so the dip line-shape is mimicked by rotational modulation/aliases of the star, not a planet on target.
